title: Jumper Cap / Capacity Jumper Error
shortDescription: Indoor unit cannot detect its capacity jumper cap on the PCB.
fullDescription:
C5 indicates that the capacity jumper (a small plastic cap installed on the PCB) is missing, damaged, or installed incorrectly. The PCB uses this jumper to identify the indoor unit's capacity (9k, 12k, 18k, 24k BTU).

Without this jumper the unit refuses to operate. The cap may dislodge during shipping or service work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat jumper cap
fixSteps.instruction: Open electrical cover; find the JUMP/Cap marked connector and reseat the plastic jumper.

whenToCallPro: If the jumper is missing entirely and replacement isn't available.

faq.a: No, the jumper is capacity-specific and keyed to the model.

title: High Pressure Protection
shortDescription: Discharge pressure has exceeded the safety threshold.
fullDescription:
E1 on Gree mini-splits means the high-pressure switch on the compressor discharge line has tripped. This typically occurs in cooling due to a dirty outdoor coil, blocked outdoor airflow, a stuck outdoor fan, or overcharge.

In heating it may indicate a blocked indoor return or very dirty filter.
symptoms: E1 after several minutes of operation
Compressor stops, fan may keep running

fixSteps.title: Clean outdoor coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse condenser fins with gentle water from inside out.

fixSteps.title: Verify outdoor fan
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm outdoor fan spins smoothly whenever compressor runs.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is good but E1 persists, a pro must check refrigerant charge.

faq.a: The safety switch protects components, but repeated trips can damage the compressor.

title: Anti-Freezing Protection (Indoor Coil Icing)
shortDescription: Indoor evaporator coil temperature is too low - icing risk.
fullDescription:
E2 on Gree units triggers when the indoor coil thermistor reads below the freeze threshold. The unit pauses cooling to let the coil warm up.

Most often caused by restricted indoor airflow - dirty filter, blocked return, low fan speed, or low refrigerant charge.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Wash reusable filters and let dry.

fixSteps.title: Check fan speed
fixSteps.instruction: Set fan to high and verify strong airflow from vanes.

fixSteps.title: Clean evaporator coil
fixSteps.instruction: Use no-rinse coil cleaner while unit is off.

whenToCallPro: Low refrigerant requires a pro with gauges and leak detection.

faq.q: Can I just turn it back on?
faq.a: Yes, but it will freeze again without fixing airflow.

title: Low Pressure Protection
shortDescription: Suction pressure is too low - usually refrigerant loss.
fullDescription:
E3 indicates low-pressure protection. The system senses inadequate suction pressure which usually means the refrigerant charge is low or the system has developed a leak.

A blocked indoor airflow in cooling mode can also trigger it, as can a stuck expansion valve.
symptoms: Warm air from vents in cooling

fixSteps.title: Check airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Clean filter and verify unobstructed return.

fixSteps.title: Professional leak test
fixSteps.instruction: HVAC tech will pressurize and leak-search the system.

whenToCallPro: Always, unless the cause is clearly airflow.

faq.a: No - it requires EPA 608 certification and leak repair first.

title: Discharge Temperature Protection
shortDescription: Compressor discharge temperature is dangerously high.
fullDescription:
E4 protects the compressor when the discharge line temperature exceeds about 115C. Usually related to low refrigerant, restricted condenser airflow, or a failing EEV.

Continued operation with this fault will destroy the compressor, so the PCB shuts down automatically.

fixSteps.title: Professional diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: A pro will check charge and discharge thermistor.

whenToCallPro: Always, unless coil cleaning fixes it.

faq.a: Not if the protection trips properly and you stop using the unit until fixed.

title: Overcurrent Protection
shortDescription: Compressor or inverter is drawing excessive current.
fullDescription:
E5 is an overcurrent trip at the inverter. Causes include high operating pressures, low supply voltage (causing higher current draw), or a failing inverter module.

On older Gree models this may indicate a failed run capacitor.
symptoms: E5 within seconds of compressor start

fixSteps.title: Verify voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure supply voltage at outdoor disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Professional diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: Tech tests IPM and compressor windings.

faq.q: Could this be from a brownout?
faq.a: Yes, low voltage is a common cause.

title: Communication Error (Indoor-Outdoor)
shortDescription: Loss of communication between indoor and outdoor units.
fullDescription:
E6 is Gree's generic communication fault. The indoor PCB cannot establish or maintain serial communication with the outdoor PCB.

Common causes: miswired terminal block, damaged interconnect cable, tripped outdoor breaker, or failed outdoor PCB.
whenToCallPro: If wiring is correct but fault persists, the outdoor PCB likely needs replacement.

faq.q: Is this the same as H6?
faq.a: No, H6 is indoor fan motor.

title: Mode Conflict (Multi-Split)
shortDescription: One indoor unit requesting heat while another requests cool on the same multi-split.
fullDescription:
E7 appears on multi-split Gree systems when two indoor units are set to opposite modes. Standard multi-splits cannot cool and heat simultaneously; all indoor units must run the same mode family.

Set all heads to the same mode or use 'Auto'/'Fan' on the conflicting unit.
symptoms: E7 on one or more indoor heads

fixSteps.title: Align modes
fixSteps.instruction: Set every indoor unit to either cool or heat (not a mix).

faq.a: Yes, only the mode (heat/cool) must match.

title: High Temperature / Overload Protection
shortDescription: Indoor or outdoor has triggered a high-temperature overload.
fullDescription:
E8 is a generic overheat protection on the indoor coil or outdoor unit. In heat mode it often indicates restricted indoor airflow causing the coil to exceed temperature limits.

Clean the filter, check return airflow, and retry.

fixSteps.title: Verify fan
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure indoor fan reaches high speed.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is fine and fault persists, call a pro for sensor diagnostics.

faq.a: Heat mode runs the coil hot, so airflow issues trip the high-limit faster.

title: Defrost Mode Active
shortDescription: The system is in defrost cycle - this is normal operation.
fullDescription:
H1 is informational, not an error. In heating, when the outdoor coil ices up, the system reverses to cooling mode briefly to melt ice. During defrost H1 shows and the indoor fan pauses.

It typically lasts 3-10 minutes and clears automatically.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Let the defrost cycle finish - 3-10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: If constant
fixSteps.instruction: If H1 runs every few minutes, call a pro to check refrigerant and reversing valve.

whenToCallPro: Only if defrost runs excessively often.

faq.a: No - it's a normal status indicator.

title: Electrostatic Dust Collector Fault
fullDescription:
H2 signals a problem with the optional electrostatic dust collector (on some premium Gree models). Typically a dirty collector or dislodged connector.

Removing and cleaning the filter usually resolves it.

fixSteps.title: Remove filter
fixSteps.instruction: Slide out the electrostatic filter and rinse.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall
fixSteps.instruction: Dry completely and reinstall, ensuring contacts seat firmly.

faq.a: Yes, you can remove the module if it's faulty.

title: Compressor Overload Protection
fullDescription:
H3 shows when the compressor's internal klixon overload trips. This is usually due to high head pressure, low voltage, or a tiring compressor.

Allow 30 minutes for the overload to reset and investigate root cause.

faq.q: How often is compressor the issue?
faq.a: Usually pressure/airflow - compressor replacement is a last resort.

title: System Overload
fullDescription:
H4 represents a broader overload condition on Gree systems, often logged after multiple related trips (like several E1 or E4 events). The unit locks out until manually reset.

Clear by cycling main power for 10 minutes and investigating airflow and charge.

fixSteps.title: Address airflow
fixSteps.instruction: Clean filters and outdoor coil before restarting.

whenToCallPro: If it returns quickly after reset.

faq.a: To force user intervention after repeated protection trips.

title: IPM Module Protection
shortDescription: The inverter IPM module has tripped a protection circuit.
fullDescription:
H5 is an IPM (Intelligent Power Module) protection event. The IPM drives the inverter compressor and includes protections for overcurrent, overtemperature, and undervoltage.

Root causes include a dirty outdoor heatsink, low incoming voltage, or a genuinely failing IPM.
safetyWarning: Dangerous DC voltage in the inverter - wait 10 minutes after power off.
symptoms: H5 within seconds of compressor start

fixSteps.title: Blow out outdoor unit
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air to clear dust from the outdoor PCB heatsink.

whenToCallPro: If heatsink is clean and voltage is fine.

faq.a: No - it's replaced as part of the outdoor PCB.

title: Indoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Indoor fan motor not running or no speed feedback.
fullDescription:
H6 on Gree systems means the indoor fan is not spinning or the PCB isn't getting feedback. Causes include obstructed blower wheel, failed motor, or PCB drive fault.

It's one of the most common Gree codes and often caused by pet hair jamming the blower wheel.

fixSteps.title: Inspect blower
fixSteps.instruction: Remove front panel, spin blower by hand.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If bearings are stiff, replace fan motor.

faq.q: Can I clean the wheel without removing it?
faq.a: Partially, but a thorough cleaning needs wheel removal.

title: Limited Frequency Operation - Overload
fullDescription: The unit has detected an overload condition and reduced compressor frequency to protect itself.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: F6 shown on display or remote
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

title: Outdoor Defrost Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The outdoor defrost coil sensor is open or shorted.
fullDescription: Gree dE indicates the defrost thermistor on the outdoor coil failed.

faq.a: Mainly — defrost is a heat-mode function.

title: Compressor Start-up Failure
shortDescription: Compressor failed to start during start-up sequence.
fullDescription: Gree Lc indicates the compressor did not start — stuck rotor, inverter fault, or wiring.

fixSteps.title: Tech inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Service tech checks inverter and compressor windings.

title: Phase Sequence Error
fullDescription: Gree Ld (on three-phase units only) indicates the phase rotation is reversed at the disconnect.

fixSteps.title: Swap two phases
fixSteps.instruction: Have an electrician swap any two phases at the disconnect.

faq.q: Can a single-phase unit get Ld?

safetyWarning: Phase work requires a licensed electrician.

title: Compressor Model Mismatch
shortDescription: Outdoor PCB does not recognize compressor model.
fullDescription: Gree Le indicates the PCB read a compressor model code that does not match the configuration.

fixSteps.title: Verify part numbers
fixSteps.instruction: Compare PCB and compressor model numbers.

faq.a: Yes — wrong replacement parts cause this.

title: Indoor-Outdoor Mismatch
shortDescription: Indoor and outdoor unit capacities do not match.
fullDescription: Gree Lp indicates the connected indoor and outdoor capacities are incompatible (e.g., 9k indoor on 24k outdoor without a brancher).

faq.a: Only on multi-zone outdoor with proper branch box.
